name: Risperidone
summary: An atypical antipsychotic with potent D2 blockade; dose-related EPS and prolactin elevation are its main drawbacks.
mechanism: Antagonizes D2 and 5-HT2A receptors (plus α1 and H1); high 5-HT2A-to-D2 ratio at low doses.

dosing.adult: 1–6 mg/day (start 1–2 mg; usual 2–6 mg for schizophrenia)
dosing.maxDose: 6 mg/day in most practice (label permits up to 16 mg)

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; third-trimester exposure can cause neonatal EPS or withdrawal.
safety.lactation: Present in breast milk; limited data.
warnings: Boxed warning (antipsychotics): increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
Hyperprolactinemia — galactorrhea, sexual dysfunction, bone effects
EPS is dose-related — use the lowest effective dose
Moderate weight gain and metabolic effects
safety.overdose: Sedation, tachycardia, hypotension, and EPS; QT prolongation at high doses.

clinicalPearls: The active metabolite 9-hydroxyrisperidone is renally cleared — reduce the dose in renal impairment.
EPS and prolactin elevation exceed other atypicals; keep the dose low.
good: Psychosis or mania needing potent D2 blockade, with a long-acting injectable available.
bad: Patients sensitive to EPS or prolactin-related side effects, or with significant renal impairment.
